benchmark_eval.summary: The paper presents an empirical audit of 26 frozen data-science benchmark releases, separately measuring artifact accessibility, evaluation reconstructability from public documentation, and CPU-only evaluator executability via a two-pass smoke test. It finds accessibility is near-universal but reconstructability (50%) and executability (27%) drop sharply, attributing gaps mainly to undocumented predictions-to-score mappings and runtime credential/environment dependencies, and releases the full evidence corpus.

concerns.issue: Inter-coder reliability on the five R2 criteria is low (α=0.434), yet these criteria define the headline 50% reconstructability figure; adjudication is by another LLM with no human ground-truth check.
concerns.suggested_fix: Validate a stratified subsample against human expert coding to calibrate the LLM-adjudicated labels before reporting R2 as a headline endpoint.

concerns.issue: All coding and adjudication are performed by LLM instances; the paper reports agreement between models but never accuracy against any independent gold standard.
concerns.suggested_fix: Report precision/recall of adjudicated labels against a small human-annotated gold subset, not solely inter-model agreement.

concerns.issue: 'Minimal repair' is explicitly a judgment call, yet it changes E3(any) from 5/26 to 7/26 (a 40% relative shift) on the primary endpoint, with no objective repair-effort threshold defined ex ante.
concerns.suggested_fix: Pre-register a concrete repair-effort rubric (e.g., lines changed, time budget) rather than a post hoc qualitative description.

concerns.issue: With N=26 and sparse category cells (e.g., text2sql R2=1/5), category-level E3 proportions and the R2-E3 odds ratio (10.3) are statistically fragile despite being flagged as exploratory in text.
concerns.suggested_fix: Add explicit exploratory-only caveats directly in Table 2/3 captions, not only in prose.

concerns.issue: Table 3's 'R2 crit' column (count of non-blocking vs. satisfied criteria) is never defined in the caption or body text, requiring readers to reverse-engineer its meaning from the permissive rule.
concerns.suggested_fix: Add an explicit column definition to the table caption.

concerns.issue: Novelty argument is well-articulated against BetterBench/BenchmarkCards/EvalCards but omits comparison to ACM/IEEE artifact-evaluation badge methodology, which also does frozen-commit execution checks.
concerns.suggested_fix: Add explicit contrast with artifact-evaluation badge criteria in the related-work or novelty-matrix figure.

repro_stats.summary: The paper audits 26 frozen benchmark releases for data-science tasks, decomposing 'reproducibility' into accessibility, reconstructability (R2), and CPU-only evaluator executability (E3), scored via a two-coder LLM codebook and a preregistered two-pass smoke test. It reports accessibility near-universal, R2 at 50%, and E3 at 27%, releasing the full evidence trail, labels, logs, and patches.

concerns.issue: Both 'independent' coders and the adjudicator are LLM instances from the same model family (Claude variants), not human annotators; correlated blind spots across same-vendor models undermine the validity of Krippendorff/Gwet statistics as evidence of task difficulty rather than shared model bias.
concerns.suggested_fix: Add a human-coder validation subsample (even partial, e.g. 8-10 releases) to check whether model-model disagreement patterns match human-model disagreement.

concerns.issue: Primary R2/E3 outcomes rest entirely on adjudicated labels from a third LLM (opus-4), with no independent check on adjudicator accuracy, despite nominal alpha (0.434) falling well below the paper's own 0.80 target.
concerns.suggested_fix: Report R2/E3 endpoints computed separately per raw coder (not just adjudicated) to bound how much the headline 50%/27% figures shift under plausible relabeling.

concerns.issue: Table 2 reports category-level R2/E3 proportions (e.g., 0% text2sql, 50% tabular) with n as low as 4-5 and no confidence intervals, inviting readers to treat these as stable category differences despite the text elsewhere correctly flagging category comparisons as exploratory.
concerns.suggested_fix: Add Wilson CIs to Table 2 or explicitly annotate cells with n<8 as indicative only, consistent with the exploratory framing used in Section 5.6.

concerns.issue: Several corpus entries share authorship/lineage (Spider, Spider2.0, Spider2-V; BIRD, BIRD-CRITIC; DS-1000 vs. PandasEval/NumpyEval CERT), so failures may cluster by codebase family rather than being independent draws, yet Wilson and bootstrap CIs treat all 26 as exchangeable units.
concerns.suggested_fix: Report a lineage-clustered or leave-one-family-out sensitivity check on the primary E3 CI.

concerns.issue: The claim-evidence concordance analysis (2/14 runnable-as-framed) is another small-subgroup inference layered atop an already small corpus, compounding multiple-small-N comparisons across the results section without any correction or pooled uncertainty accounting.
concerns.suggested_fix: State explicitly that this and other subgroup statistics are descriptive only, and consider a single combined uncertainty statement covering all subgroup claims.

concerns.issue: Reporting both nominal (0.434) and post-hoc ordinal (0.660) Krippendorff's alpha without prespecifying which is authoritative reads as reliability-metric shopping, even though both are disclosed transparently.
concerns.suggested_fix: State in advance (or clearly mark as post-hoc) that the ordinal analysis is a secondary robustness check, not an alternative headline reliability figure.

skeptical_kdd.summary: The paper conducts a manual/LLM-coded audit of 26 frozen data-science foundation-model benchmark releases, separating artifact accessibility, evaluation-reconstructability (via a codebook scored by two LLM coders and adjudicated by a third), and evaluator executability (via a preregistered CPU-only, zero-inference two-pass smoke test). It reports that accessibility is near-universal but reconstructability (50%/11.5% under permissive/conservative rules) and executability (26.9%/19.2%) are much lower, and releases the full evidence trail, logs, and patches.

concerns.issue: The headline reconstructability endpoint (R2, 50.0%/11.5%) rests on labels from two LLM 'coders' and an LLM adjudicator, with observed reliability far below the paper's own preregistered target (Krippendorff's alpha nominal 0.434 vs. target 0.80, only 59% raw agreement on 156 cells). The paper is candid about this, but a primary quantitative claim built on adjudicated labels from a process that fails its own preregistered reliability bar is a serious validity threat, not just a caveat — every adjudicated cell was a coin-flip-adjacent disagreement resolved by a third model with no independent check on the adjudicator's own reliability.
concerns.suggested_fix: Report an inter-rater reliability figure for the adjudicator against a human-coded subsample, or recruit at least one human coder for a meaningful stratified subset (e.g., 8-10 releases) to calibrate the LLM-only pipeline before treating R2 counts as a scientific finding rather than a demonstration.

concerns.issue: No human coder or human adjudicator is used anywhere in the audit; the entire reliability/adjudication apparatus is LLM-on-LLM. For a paper whose central thesis concerns trust in AI-generated/AI-evaluated measurement, relying exclusively on non-human, potentially non-reproducible, closed model snapshots (claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-opus-4) to produce the paper's own 'ground truth' labels is a notable and somewhat self-undermining methodological gap that is flagged in Limitations but not mitigated anywhere in the study.
concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least a partial human-annotation validation study, or substantially soften claims (e.g., avoid presenting R2 percentages to one decimal place as if precise) until human validation exists.

concerns.issue: Corpus size (N=26) is small, and per-category cells are tiny (text2sql n=5, tabular n=4, code-gen n=4), yet the paper reports category-level E3 proportions (e.g., tabular 50%, text2sql 0%) and an OR≈10.3 R2-E3 association prominently in the abstract/results despite explicitly non-significant p-values (0.073, 0.28). Although labeled 'exploratory,' these numbers will likely be quoted out of context (e.g., 'no text-to-SQL evaluator executes') as if generalizable, which is not statistically supportable at this N.
concerns.suggested_fix: De-emphasize category-level percentages in the abstract/headline text; report them only with explicit small-n caveats attached at point of use, and avoid stating category conclusions ('No text-to-SQL evaluator ran to a score') as flat claims when n=5.

concerns.issue: Corpus construction (35 candidates, 9 excluded for failure to resolve an official artifact 'under standard repository paths within this pass') is a subjective, single-pass screening step performed by the same team that then reports on artifact accessibility as a key outcome. This creates potential selection bias: benchmarks that are harder to find quickly are dropped before the accessibility/reconstructability analysis even begins, which could inflate the A0=A1=26/26 saturation finding and is not independently auditable from the manuscript alone (only search keywords are given, not the actual exclusion ledger contents).
concerns.suggested_fix: Report the 9 excluded benchmarks by name and reason in the paper body (not just 'released with the artifact'), and discuss whether their exclusion is correlated with the very accessibility/documentation properties being measured.

concerns.issue: The contribution is fundamentally a checklist/audit of pre-existing third-party benchmarks rather than a new dataset, benchmark, or method — its value to the broader KDD audience depends entirely on whether the community treats 'meta-benchmarking of reproducibility' as core versus niche. The paper's own related-work section frames its delta over BetterBench/MEQA/EvalCards mainly as 'we execute code and pin commits' rather than a new measurement construct, which is a real but incremental methodological contribution, not a new capability or resource for building/using benchmarks going forward beyond the recommendations list.
concerns.suggested_fix: Strengthen the case for downstream utility beyond documentation — e.g., show that the released pipeline was actually adopted/reused, or that the audit changed a benchmark's practice, to demonstrate impact beyond a one-time audit.

concerns.issue: Claims that comprehensive artifacts (registry, evidence records, raw/adjudicated labels, execution logs, patches, analysis pipeline) are 'released' cannot be verified from the manuscript text; no persistent identifier, DOI, or repository link is given in the provided material.
concerns.suggested_fix: Include a concrete, verifiable link/DOI to the released resource in the camera-ready version so reviewers and readers can confirm the artifacts exist and match the described schema.

concerns.issue: The definition of 'minimal repair' is explicitly acknowledged as a judgment call that could shift 2 of the 26 outcomes; while transparently reported, this means the primary E3 endpoint (7/26) has a soft boundary that a different auditor could reasonably move, undercutting the crispness suggested by presenting E3 to one decimal-percent precision.
concerns.suggested_fix: Report E3 as a range (5-9/26 depending on repair-strictness) alongside the point estimate to reflect this acknowledged subjectivity.

concerns.issue: The 'novelty matrix' figure comparing this work against prior frameworks (BetterBench, MEQA, EvalCards, etc.) is self-constructed and self-scored ('as described in its own paper'), which is a common but weak form of positioning evidence.
concerns.suggested_fix: Have this comparison checked by, or explicitly solicit feedback from, authors of at least one compared framework, or cite independent characterizations of those frameworks' methods.

concerns.issue: Percentages are frequently reported to one decimal place (e.g., 59.0%, 26.9%) despite N=26, which overstates precision relative to the width of the accompanying confidence intervals.
concerns.suggested_fix: Round headline percentages to the nearest whole percent, or consistently foreground the CI rather than the point estimate.
